source.title: Flat Channels to Infinity in Neural Loss Landscapes
source.authors: Flavio Martinelli; Alexander van Meegen; Berfin Şimşek; W. Gerstner; Johanni Brea

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies channels to infinity in regression loss landscapes. Its results do not test the listed classification-error, width-versus-spurious-minima, shortcut, initialization-comparison, above-stability recovery, or batch-normalization versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports gradient-based training outcomes in regression, including reaching channels and optimizer stalling at their entrance. These bear on the broader topic but do not measure the behavior named by any listed version. It also cites related prior-work results, which are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Section 4 and Figure 6d report an original full-batch GD result on sharpness reaching 2/η, bearing on V5's edge-of-stability component in a new toy regression setting. They do not test recovery above the initial stability limit.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. Gradient-based training frequently enters channels in the tested regression MLPs; the channels approach gated-linear-unit functions and can lead to minima at infinity. Finite-step optimizers can stall early. General convergence to minima at infinity remains a hypothesis supported empirically, with stability established in the toy example; occurrence in large-scale architectures remains unquantified.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments use gradient flow, SGD, or ADAM on regression loss landscapes to study channels to infinity, rather than the listed classification-error, width, shortcut, initialization-comparison, above-stability recovery, or normalization recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Channel frequency increases with GP kernel scale; in the toy example, finite-step SGD and ADAM get stuck early in channels at the edge of stability.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient flow reaches channels from random initialization across the tested regression settings; channel frequency increases with target roughness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Smooth-activation regression MLPs can enter channels to infinity under gradient flow, with frequency depending on the target function.

fits_no_version.finding: Minibatch SGD and Adam enter channels but stall early in the two-neuron erf example.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Finite-step stochastic optimizers can make limited progress along extremely flat regression channels despite continued progress under gradient flow.

record.problems: Channel probabilities are presented qualitatively in the supplied text; the relevant figure values are not stated numerically. The detailed SGD/ADAM stalling result is a single toy regression example, and no uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows retained for finite-norm minima versus channel loss distributions or Hessian-eigenvalue distributions: the text describes these as similar loss distributions and sharper-but-flatter channel geometry, but they do not measure a listed claim version or add a separate gradient-training outcome beyond the channel results recorded here. Figure-only frequency values were not reconstructed.

untested.parts: CIFAR classification training error, label corruption, and model-size, stopping, and regularization comparisons.
Realizable ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious-minimum frequencies across matched widths, and extra-student-neuron comparisons.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts, special initialization of deep plain networks, and normalization-free residual training.
Initialization comparisons for training speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth.

Wide-network recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, initial loss spikes and curvature drops, divergence boundaries, below-threshold initialization followed by divergence, and sustained loss reduction over long times at the threshold.
Batch-normalization and Fixup comparisons for training speed, stability, and learning-rate tolerance.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V5. Threshold-limited progress does not establish that loss stops decreasing entirely, so a challenges verdict is unwarranted.

versions.untested_parts: Classification training error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, and the stated size, stopping, and regularization comparisons.
Teacher-student ReLU spurious-minimum frequency as widths grow, and the effect of giving the student extra neurons.
Depth-related classification training error in plain versus residual networks, and the stated special-initialization and normalization-free residual comparisons.
Comparisons of initialization schemes for training speed or trainable depth, including the stated orthogonal, Gaussian, and convolutional settings.

Recovery at learning rates above the initial stability limit and the stated sharpness-threshold or divergence comparisons. The paper discusses edge-of-stability stalling in a toy regression example, without testing the version's above-limit recovery claim.
Batch-normalization comparisons for training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and the stated Fixup comparison.

rows.subject: MLPs (4420 networks, aggregate)
rows.size_stated: Architectures varied; 1 hidden layer with 2, 4, 8, or 16 neurons, plus deeper MLPs with 2 or 3 hidden layers of 4 neurons
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient flow from random Glorot normal initializations on modified Rosenbrock and Gaussian-process regression datasets; trajectories classified for channel convergence.

conditions.value: modified Rosenbrock and four Gaussian processes with kernel scaling s ∈ {0.1, 0.5, 2, 10}
softplus and erf; deep Rosenbrock networks used softplus
50 fits per configuration with different random initializations

rows.measure: Estimated probability of converging to a channel to infinity
rows.baseline: Finite-norm local minima are the comparison group; no probability value stated
rows.value: A substantial probability of reaching channels in all tested datasets
rows.note: The paper states that 4420 networks were trained in total. The channel probability is described qualitatively in the text; precise plotted values are not transcribed.
rows.check: Channel frequency measures none of the listed versions. The reported channel occurrence is supported, but cannot establish a version's effect.

rows.subject: MLPs (GP dataset runs; aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Compared channel-convergence frequency across Gaussian-process target functions with different kernel scaling.
rows.baseline: Lower kernel scaling settings; exact values not stated
rows.value: More channels are found when the target function is rough; channel frequency has a positive correlation with GP kernel scale s
rows.note: The text gives a qualitative relationship; it does not provide individual frequency values.
rows.check: The relationship between target roughness and channel frequency measures none of the listed versions.

rows.subject: Two-neuron erf network
rows.operation_detail: Compared SGD and ADAM trajectories with gradient flow on a two-neuron regression toy example.

conditions.value: Fit a one-dimensional erf target function
4096 fixed standard normally distributed input samples for finite-data curves
default parameters η = 0.001, β1 = 0.9, β2 = 0.999, ϵ = 10−8; batchsize 16

rows.measure: Progress along the channel toward the minimum at infinity
rows.baseline: Gradient flow continues slowly along the channel; exact comparison value not stated
rows.value: SGD and ADAM get stuck early in the channels
rows.locator: Section 4, Figure 6b and Figure 6d; Appendix C.5
rows.note: The authors attribute the finite-step-size limit to reaching the edge of stability.
rows.check: The reported SGD and Adam stalling is supported, but these minibatch runs test neither above-initial-limit recovery nor V5's full-batch dynamics.

rows.subject: Two-neuron erf network
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed maximum Hessian eigenvalue during finite-step-size gradient descent along a channel.
rows.measure: Maximum Hessian eigenvalue at the edge of stability
rows.value: λmax = 2/η; along the channel, λmax ∼ 1/ϵ2 and ϵmin ∼ √η
rows.note: This is an edge-of-stability analysis in the toy regression setting, not a test of recovery from learning rates above the initial stability limit.
rows.check: The reader overlooks V5's separate edge-of-stability component. Figure 6d reports finite-step GD reaching λmax = 2/η and limiting further channel progress. This establishes threshold behavior, but not the complete sustained-loss-decrease behavior. Specify full-batch GD; the 2/η threshold should not be attributed directly to Adam.

relationships.reason: R4 reaches sharpness 2/η, but Section 4 and Figure 6d describe this threshold as limiting channel progress, with εmin proportional to √η; the result qualifies productive edge-of-stability dynamics in this setting.
relationships.display_finding: Sharpness reached 2/η, where further channel progress was limited by ε_min proportional to √η.
